newsitem.title: UK: UK's Crest share settlement system faces new delay.
newsitem.headline: UK's Crest share settlement system faces new delay.

text.p: Executives running the UK's new electronic share settlement system Crest on Thursday denied the system was in crisis but confirmed they will review the April deadline for a full transition to the new paperless regime.

Four months after Crest was first used to settle trades in a selected number of shares, CrestCo chief executive Iain Saville responded to reports of delays and inefficiencies in the system and said most users are coping with the transition quite well.
He said only a few were having difficulties either because of inadequate software or a lack of user expertise.

But he said the board of directors of CrestCo, a Bank of England-led consortium of 60 financial institutions, will soon review the April deadline for a full transition to Crest from the stock exchange's existing Talisman paper-based system.

The problems are embarrassing for Crestco, which was set up in 1993 following the collapse of the previous Taurus project, led by the London Stock Exchange, to develop a computerised system for recording the ownership of shares.
Taurus was abandoned in 1993 after running up costs of some 38 million stg, a failure which led to the departure of the London Stock Exchange's then chief executive Peter Rawlins.
The Bank of England set up a task force to design and develop an alternative, eventually coming up with Crest.
Yet CrestCo said earlier this month the transition of around 10 FTSE 100 stocks to the new regime was being put back to 1997 from next month after software teething problems.
And today's hastily-convened press conference was in response to reports of mounting complaints over the system from top brokerages.

"I think the exchange and Crest gave people enough time (to prepare for the transition), but when it came down to the crunch, a lot of people -- especially the smaller firms -- just weren't geared up," said one senior share trader.

Speaking at CrestCo's office in London, Saville said the main question the board has to consider when it meets on November 25 is, "are there enough slow ships in the convoy" that would justify pushing back the April deadline, Saville said.

He said that some of Crest's software glitches have been rectified during the past two weeks, enabling Crest to process settlements more quickly and avert the kind of backlogs that plagued the system in late October.
Saville said other problems are still being addressed, but users also need to get their inhouse systems in place and get over the "learning curve" of handling the new system.
David Jones, chief executive of discount brokerage Sharelink, also a board member of Crest, said he has noticed improvements in the system during the last couple of weeks.

"But it's not just Crest ... across the industry people are starting to understand how to use the system and that has helped," Jones said. "People need time to learn how to use it before the volumes get too high."
